description: Realistic tasks an agent is asked to do on the example sets, run through Claude Code with the fastart skill (evals/run.mjs). Each lists the set it copies, the prompt, and a check: a file that must validate and a predicate on it. Compare tokens and turns before and after a tooling change.

tasks.prompt: In dog.fart, add a clip named blink that closes and opens the eyes (scale the eye parts down and back) over a quarter second. Validate the file when done.
In ships/fighter.fart, make the thrust state a little more dramatic: widen the wings by posing wing_l and wing_r outward in that state only. Keep every other state as it is.
In crate.fart, give the crate's mesh one level of smoothing and smooth normals so it reads rounded, and add a short clip named settle that squashes it slightly then returns.
Add a new prop: pickups/battery.fart, a small battery with a body and a glowing cap that follows the project's direction (read style.gas first). Give it an idle state and a pulse clip.
In face.fart, add a viseme state named U (lips pushed forward and narrow) by morphing the mouth path, and put it into the speak clip between O and E.
Make a new palette file palettes/rust.fart with the same slot names as palettes/hull.fart but in rusted browns and oranges, and link it from ships/drone.fart instead of hull.fart.
Add a second sweep to vase.fart: a lid, a lathe with a knob on top, in the clay colour, sitting on the rim. Keep it a sweep so the profile stays editable.
Tell me, without changing anything, which parts of ships/cruiser.fart have anchors and what the longest clip is.
